title: What If Earth's Day Lasted 25 Hours?

scenes.text: What if a day lasted 25 hours? The Moon is already doing it.
Earth's day stretches by about 1.7 milliseconds every century.
The Moon pulls tidal bulges in the ocean, and those bulges drag against Earth's spin like a brake.
Meanwhile the Moon drifts away from us by about 3.8 centimeters every year.
Go back 68 million years and a T. rex day was about 20 minutes shorter. In the Cambrian it was only around 21 hours.
One extra hour would take hundreds of millions of years. So no clock will ever jump. The slowdown just keeps going.

description:
What if a day on Earth lasted 25 hours?
It is slowly happening because the Moon brakes Earth's spin, but the extra hour is hundreds of millions of years away.
What should we run through next?
